item.title: Meta AI Chief Posts Deep‑Fake Video Featuring OpenAI CEO
item.description:
Meta AI Chief Posts Deep‑Fake Video Featuring OpenAI CEO

Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, posted an AI‑generated clip on Instagram showing himself, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Muse’s mascot Jolly in a four‑way video call.

🔍 Overview

  • Wang’s clip was released on Instagram.
  • The video shows a four‑way call between Wang, Zuckerberg, Altman, and Jolly.
  • Altman is dressed as Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint.
  • Caption reads: “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” referencing the AI agent race.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The clip is labeled as AI content in accordance with Meta’s AI policy.
  • Meta requires AI‑generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI; static images have no such requirement.
  • Wang’s post complies with this labeling rule.

👇 Context

  • Instagram has faced criticism for allowing AI‑generated images that lack disclosure, such as an AI image of actress Mia Goth shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge.
  • Meta previously removed accounts that posed as others and used their likenesses.
  • OpenAI’s Sora app made Sam Altman’s likeness available for AI content generation, leading to quickly flooded fake Altman videos.

🪄 Commentary

  • Wang has heavily promoted Muse on social media, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to traditional marketers as “corposlops.”
  • A major tech executive posting a deep‑fake of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that has been criticized for its handling of AI‑generated content.

📈 Implications

  • The incident highlights the differing platform policies on labeling AI‑generated media.
  • It underscores the need for consistent disclosure requirements across video and image content.

#Meta #AIvideo #Deepfake

Source: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram

item.title: AI‑altered White House renovation photo posted by Donald Trump flagged by Google detector
item.description:
AI‑altered White House renovation photo posted by Donald Trump flagged by Google detector

President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing off renovations to the White House — but one of them appears to be modified with AI.

🔍 Overview

  • The post includes a “before and after” photo of a freshly painted White House column.
  • The image was shared to brag about White House restoration work.

🧩 Detection

  • Google’s AI detector flagged the picture as “made or edited with OpenAI.”
  • The Verge confirmed the photo is flagged as AI‑generated when uploaded to Google’s SynthID Detector, which scans for an invisible watermark indicating it was “created or edited” with AI.
  • The SynthID watermark was not detected on other pictures Trump posted, which show the White House façade and heliport.

⚙️ Visual anomalies

  • Reddit users noted an uneven number of steps on both sides of the structure.
  • The number of steps does not match the ones in the “before” photo.
  • The before and after photos appear nearly identical in angle and detail; the reflection in the windows is nearly the same, and the protective cardboard at the bottom of the column seems to be in the same spot as well.
  • The “newly‑painted” column looks unnaturally smooth.

📚 Context

  • Real pictures show people painting the front of the White House in June, so it’s possible the column actually did get a fresh coat of paint — the White House didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
  • Trump is no stranger to AI tools, as he often posts AI‑generated caricatures of himself.
  • The White House has previously posted racist AI memes and at least one photo deceptively edited to make a protester appear distraught.

#AI #Deepfake #Trump #WhiteHouse

Source: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work

item.title: Google Releases SynthID Detector; Microsoft Teams to Add Deepfake Detection
item.description:
Google Releases SynthID Detector; Microsoft Teams to Add Deepfake Detection

Google has made its SynthID Detector available to the public, and Microsoft announced that Teams will support third‑party deep‑fake detection beginning in November.

🔍 Overview

  • Google opened SynthID Detector to the public.
  • Microsoft Teams will support third‑party deep‑fake detection, expected in November.

⚙️ Key details

  • SynthID Detector is a tool that identifies synthetic media; it is now publicly accessible.
  • Teams integration will allow users to leverage external deep‑fake detection services.

📅 Availability

  • Google’s SynthID Detector: currently public.
  • Microsoft Teams deep‑fake detection: slated for November.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides organizations and individuals with means to verify authenticity of audio/video content.
  • Addresses growing concerns about AI‑generated deepfakes used in misinformation and legal contexts.

#AI #deepfake #privacy #Microsoft #Google

Source: Weekly Letter to Our EDRM Global Community – 13 October 2026
